title: Efficient machine for masked selection
statement: Let $M$ map pairs of bit strings to a bit, and suppose the verifier that returns $M(x,r)$ is efficient in the specified polynomial-time model. For any natural numbers $a,k$, there are natural numbers $K,e$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ such that, for every input $x$, there are a natural number $s$ and a Boolean mask whose number of true entries is $a(|x|+1)^k$, with $s+|\mathrm{mask}|\le K(|x|^e+1)$. On every choice word $w$ of length exactly $K(|x|^e+1)$, $N$ halts, outputs the one-bit word whose bit is $M(x,u)$ for $u$ obtained by applying the mask to the length-$|\mathrm{mask}|$ segment of $w$ beginning at position $s$, and that selected word has length $a(|x|+1)^k$.
hypotheses_covered: The verifier returning $M(x,r)$ is efficient in the specified polynomial-time model
$M$ is a map from pairs of bit strings to a bit
